purpose: P1.5 probe references. NOT SHIPPED CONTENT. Not signer-reviewed.

B.description: Flat hand, fingers extended and together, thumb folded across the palm.

U.description: Index and middle extended and together; ring and little folded down.

V.description: Index and middle extended and spread apart; ring and little folded down.

W.description: Index, middle and ring extended and spread; little folded; thumb holds it.

C.description: Fingers curved into a C with a visible gap; thumb opposed, not touching.

O.description: All fingers and thumb form a closed circle; the thumb touches the fingertips.

A.description: Fist with the thumb alongside, not across. The ambiguity is thumb position: alongside and across both read as a closed hand.

M.description: Three fingers folded over the thumb. Depth-ambiguous: the tips sit ON the thumb, which a joint-only sensor reports as 'folded', same as A or S.

N.description: Two fingers over the thumb with the ring and little loosely curled. Differs from M by one stacked finger - a CONTACT difference, which a joint-only sensor may be unable to see at all. The probe measures whether it can; if the two land inside the lock threshold, that is the finding.

T.description: Thumb tucked between index and middle. Inter-finger depth: the thumb is hidden, and hiding is exactly what a joint-only sensor cannot report.

R.description: Index and middle extended and CROSSED. Crossing is a rotation about the finger's own axis; a joint-only format cannot express it, so this reference is an approximation and the probe treats a low score here with suspicion.

S.description: Fist with the thumb across the front of the fingers. The classic thumbs-alongside / thumbs-across ambiguity against A.

D.description: Index extended; middle, ring and little curved to meet the thumb tip. Two contacts the sensor cannot resolve.

E.description: Fingers curled so the tips rest on the thumb. Every tip is at the same place, which is the hardest thing a joint-only sensor has to see.

F.description: Index tip meets the thumb tip in a ring; middle, ring and little stay extended. The index–thumb contact makes the index look shorter.

G.description: Index points sideways with the thumb parallel to it. Orientation-dependent: the same joint angles read as different letters depending on wrist rotation.

I.description: Little finger extended; the other three folded; thumb across them.

L.description: Index up, thumb out at right angles to it; the other three folded.

X.description: Index hooked at the proximal joint; the others folded. A bent finger is a clean rotation, so this one should survive if the tracker is honest.

Y.description: Thumb and little extended, the middle three folded. Two ends of the hand at once, which is a good test of whether the tracker keeps the little finger's abduction.
